newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index close sharply lower.

text.p: Manila share index finished 33.10 points lower, or 1.12 percent, at 2,927.87 on Thursday wiping out gains of the past two days on across-the-board sell-off prompted initially by PLDT's drop in New York, traders said.
"All the bad news we've had over the past two weeks came into play today and most investors decided to sell off," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
Value turnover remained modest at 2.05 billion pesos.
The Dow's 93-point gain failed to perk up the market which instead focused on the loss of PLDT's ADR in New York.
Traders said the $0 3/8 fall of PLDT in Wall Street was not significant but prevailing bearish sentiment in the market made it susceptible to the negative news.
Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities, said scepticism in the market was helped by the continued perception of a glut in the property market.

"We see the market bouncing within the 2,900 to 2,970 range. It will take a combination of good macroeconomic news and corporate disclosures to get this market out of the doldrums," said Caesar Tanquingcen, trader at Connell Securities.
